::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 10th [1867]  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95
:::

My dear [Miss Poole](people/person_1187.qmd),
I shall be delighted to put in the history of poor Rosa’s dream, only I must let a few [numbers](organizations/other_52.qmd) go by first, or I shall by [*sic*] inundated with dreams. The [gates of Paradise](other_books/otherbook_483.qmd) have set one [lady](people/person_749.qmd) dreaming already, and the [Dreams of the Dead](other_books/otherbook_501.qmd) [another](people/person_778.qmd), and I think I must let those wait a few months or we shall fall into a universal visionary mood—but I do like the story very much and shall be glad to keep it. It is very like a sailor story I know to be true, but the odd thing there was that the man [ . . . ] drowned and having promised to appear to his aunt he <u>did</u> appear to his wife. I wonder if Rosa’s dream though at morning instead of sunset, was right as to real time.

I should think it must have been like that ghost in India, whose appearance prevented some cheat of or by the Insurance company, I forget which.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

Is East Brent still your permanent direction?

---

**Note:** Perhaps addressed to Harriet Poole (b. 1843/4), a governess. ‘Rosa’s Dream’ was not published in *MP* under that title. Part of the letter is obscured by paper pasted on the back.
